Stealth technology is used to prevent radar detection
E-glass/epoxy composite, PVC foam, and FSS are commonly used in stealth radomes
Balsa wood and PVC foam have dielectric properties closer to air
The X-band frequency range is used for measuring EM wave transmission characteristics
The formula for calculating transmission loss (L) is L = 10log(Et^2 / Ei^2)
The formula for calculating transmission rate is Transmission rate = 10L × 100%
The type 2.c sandwich construction has 8 layers of E-glass/epoxy prepreg, 6 layers of nylon/epoxy prepreg, and balsa wood as the core
The resonance frequency for type 1.a sandwich construction is 8.61 GHz
The maximum transmission rate for type 1.c sandwich construction is 89%
The bandwidth for -1 dB transmission rate for type 2.c sandwich construction is 0.74 GHz
The flexural strength of type 2.c sandwich construction is 9.84 MPa
The three-point bending test is used to measure the flexural strength of sandwich constructions
The thickness of the face material (t) in the sandwich construction is 1.008 mm
The thickness of the core material (t) in the sandwich construction is 10 mm
The dielectric constant of nylon/epoxy composite is less than that of glass/epoxy composite
The presence of balsa wood as the core increases the load-bearing capability of the sandwich construction
The free space measurement technique is used to measure the EM wave transmission characteristics
The X-band frequency range is 8.2-12.4 GHz
The transmission loss (L) is calculated using the formula L = 10log(Et^2 / Ei^2)
The transmission rate is calculated using the formula Transmission rate = 10L × 100%
The flexural strength of the sandwich construction is calculated using the formula 3PL / 2Wt^2
The three-point bending test is performed in Omega Inspection & Analytical Laboratory—Chennai, India
